subject: [Northbridge] Request: correlation-id / trace propagation feature prioritization
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Moran <alice.moran@northbridge.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: New request: correlation-id / trace propagation for Northbridge (deal NB-8342)

Team —

Quick background: Northbridge (contact: Alice Moran) has signaled that their internal auditors require end-to-end request-level provenance for any inference call that touches regulated datasets. Practically they want a customer-supplied correlation ID that: 1) is accepted via an API header, 2) is persisted to all audit logs/traces regardless of model fallback or routing, and 3) is attached as metadata to embeddings/outputs where feasible so they can reconcile vectors back to requests during audits.

This is a gating security/compliance ask for the deal. Sales is prepared to commit to a 12-month reserved capacity + implementation credits if we can deliver a supported, production-grade solution within a reasonable timeline. Alice attached the SEC questionnaire snippets that cite this requirement — forwarding the relevant PDF as an attachment.

Asking product/eng: can we scope this as a prioritized deliverable? If yes, please respond with: a) recommended implementation approach, b) rough timeline (best/expected/worst), c) interim mitigations we can offer the customer until this lands, and d) any constraints (SLA/regulatory, telemetry/backwards-compatibility) you foresee.

I know this touches routing, caching, logging, and embeddings — tagging Evelyn and Dev for scope & feasibility, Karthik for security/compliance input, and Monica to keep the commercial side aligned. Alice — I wanted to loop you in so we're all aligned on ask and timelines.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-12-02T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: New request: correlation-id / trace propagation for Northbridge (deal NB-8342)

Thanks Jordan — good summary. A few clarifying Qs before we size:

1) Scope: does Northbridge require the correlation ID to be stored with every token-level log entry (token traces/kv-cache events) or is request-level metadata sufficient (single row per request in audit logs)?
2) Embeddings: do they need the correlation ID embedded in the vector payload itself (i.e., included in the metadata field returned with an embedding), or is linkage via an external audit log acceptable?
3) Retention & access controls: are they asking for extended retention (multi-year) for correlation mappings or standard platform retention? That affects storage/archival work.

From a product perspective, this touches three systems: API surface (accept header + validation), serving runtime (ensure header propagates through routing/fallback/cache), and observability (log schema + export). We should triage with Eng to pick a short-term vs long-term approach.

Can we set a 30-minute triage this week with Dev and Security? If we can agree on scope I can produce a scoped RFC and acceptance criteria.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
PM, Redwood Console & Observability
evelyn.hart@redwood.ai
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: New request: correlation-id / trace propagation for Northbridge (deal NB-8342)

Thanks — had a quick pass with infra & runtime leads. High-level options with rough effort estimates and tradeoffs: 

Option A — Minimal (2 weeks):
- Accept X-Redwood-Correlation-Id header at the API gateway and echo into a request-level log row (per-request id, timestamp, model variant).
- DOES NOT persist id to cache metadata or embedding payloads.
- Pros: quick, low-risk; gets customer basic traceability.
- Cons: gaps when request is served from cache / routed to fallback; harder to reconcile embeddings unless we join logs.

Option B — Comprehensive (6-8 weeks):
- API header accepted + validated. Propagate header through runtime so it is attached to: request-level logs, per-token tracing events where applicable, and stored as metadata with embeddings and reranking artifacts. Ensure header persists across cache hits and model fallbacks by making it part of cache keys/metadata propagation.
- Add observability exports/filters to allow customer to query by correlation id.
- Pros: strong auditability and aligns with Northbridge ask.
- Cons: moderate infra effort; careful review needed for cache-key changes to avoid cache fragmentation. Requires coordination with logging/export infra for retention policy.

Option C — Product-building (12+ weeks):
- All of B plus: native first-class API for client-controlled provenance (signed IDs, HMAC verification), UI in Console for searching/tracking ids, and long-term retention tier for correlation mappings.
- Pros: product-grade feature for multiple customers.
- Cons: largest effort and long lead time.

Interim mitigations we can offer immediately:
- Sidecar/proxy: provide a lightweight sidecar that tags requests and pushes correlation mapping to a secure log store under NB account (short-term).
- Contractual evidence: instrumented S3 export of request logs filtered by IP/time window (manual reconciliation).

Dependencies / constraints:
- Cache key changes in Option B risk performance/cost because adding metadata to keys increases cardinality; we can instead store metadata in cache entries without changing hit logic but need a small runtime refactor.
- Retention beyond current logging SLA will require storage + legal signoff.

If Sales wants a closeable commitment this quarter, Option B is the pragmatic choice. We can scope an initial MVP of B that focuses on request+embedding metadata and leaves the Console search UI for later.

—Dev

Date: 2026-12-04T09:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: New request: correlation-id / trace propagation for Northbridge (deal NB-8342)

Appreciate the clear options. Sales talked to Alice this morning and she confirmed Northbridge can accept a comprehensive implementation (Option B) as long as we deliver within ~6 weeks and provide a compliance attestation for the delivered behavior. Commercial terms: if Redwood commits to Option B with the 6-week timeline, Northbridge will (a) sign a 12-month reserved capacity contract and (b) accept an implementation credit arrangement (details to be drafted by Monica).

Requesting a firm go/no-go on Option B by EOD Friday so I can lock the commercial commitment and update legal. If we can't commit to B, we need to present Option A + a concrete timeline for moving to B and a clear interim mitigation.

Also tagging Karthik for any security/compliance gating items we should be aware of before committing.

-Jordan
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-05T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: New request: correlation-id / trace propagation for Northbridge (deal NB-8342)

Follow-up after quick sync with runtime and infra leads. We can prioritize Option B as an expedited sprint track with the following plan and acceptance criteria: 

Plan (expedite):
- Week 0-1: Scoped RFC, security signoff (Karthik), and small schema changes for log exports.
- Week 2-4: API header + validation + propagation through routing layer and cache metadata. Embedding pipeline change to attach id as metadata when embeddings are generated.
- Week 5-6: Observability exports, query filter, and compliance attestation doc. End-to-end QA with NB sample flows.

Acceptance criteria (must be demonstrable):
- Customer can supply X-Redwood-Correlation-Id and see a matching entry in audit exports for any request, including cache hits and fallback events.
- Embeddings returned by API contain the correlation id in metadata payloads for reconciling vectors to requests.
- No regression in tail latency (+/- 5% target) on our staging perf runs for targeted workloads.

Risks & mitigations:
- Cache cardinality: will avoid embedding the id in cache key; instead store id in cache entry metadata to maintain hit rates. We'll instrument cache hit/miss to watch for fragmentation.
- Retention/exports: infra will need a short opt-in retention policy for NB; legal to approve the retention term.

We will proceed with this plan and create the RFC today. Karthik — please flag any immediate blockers on compliance. Dev — I'll add you as owner for runtime tasks in RFC; please post a short tech plan by Tuesday. Monica/Jordan — once RFC is live I'll include proposed acceptance test contents so Northbridge QA can validate.

Draft MAP attached for commercial reference.

—Evelyn
